title: Customer Momentum Brief + Renewal Scenario Bank
body:
Purpose
This is a living QBR deck template designed for two flavors: Standard (product adoption and adoption-led renewals) and Enterprise (executive summary + contractual renewal conversations). It focuses on concise executive narrative, a customer-specific momentum story, and a scenario bank of renewal conversation scripts keyed to risk scores.

Audience
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs) preparing a QBR
- Renewal/Account Execs joining the meeting
- Solutions Engineers for technical time-boxed deep dives

How to use this file
- Copy the appropriate slide set from the Standard or Enterprise folder in the Template deck.
- Plug in customer-specific metrics from the Renewal Tracker tab (see "Tracker Sample" section).
- Pick conversation script from the Scenario Bank after running the Renewal Risk Rubric.
- Use speaker notes verbatim for consistent messaging; personalize language for the relationship.

High-level deck structure (both flavors)
1) Title + One-line customer posture (30s): health status, top ask, renewal date
2) Executive summary (1 slide): ‚Outcome ask‘ (renew / no-regret next steps / executive intervention) + topline ROI statement
3) Momentum story (3 slides): adoption, feature wins, top tickets closed 
4) Business metrics (2–3 slides): usage trend, cost/unit, success KPIs (ARR impact if possible)
5) Risk & blockers (1 slide): open issues, escalation needs, timeline to mitigate
6) Roadmap alignment (1 slide): how our near-term roadmap reduces risk / increases ROI
7) Renewal options (1 slide): standard renewal, expansion, preferred enterprise terms (if applicable)
8) Ask + next steps (1 slide): clear owner + 2-week cadence items
9) Appendix: playbook snippets, technical appendix, pricing detals, legal contact

Standard variation notes
- Keep it lean (8–10 slides). Prioritize usage and time-to-value metrics.
- One-page renewal options with step-by-step next actions for self-serve customers.
- Use 30–45 minute slot default: 20 min presentation, 10–15 min discussion.

Enterprise variation notes
- Add a one-slide executive summary for the CRO/Head of AI, focused on ARR and strategic alignment.
- Include an expanded Pricing + Contract options appendix (multi-year, committed throughput discounts, dedicated capacity clauses).
- Recommended length 12–16 slides, allow 45–60 minute meeting with a 10–15 minute exec-only breakout.

Slide-by-slide example content and speaker notes (annotated)
1) Title slide
- Slide title: QBR — [Customer Name] — [Quarter]
- Speaker note: "Thanks everyone for making time. In 60 seconds: we've seen X% growth in core usage, but we have two active blockers that affect the renewal conversation. Today's goal: align on risk, agree next steps, and lock a renewal decision window."

2) Executive summary (one-slide snapshot)
- Bullets: Customer posture (Green/Amber/Red), ARR at risk, top ask, recommended renewal outcome.
- Speaker note: "Topline — we're recommending a 12-month renewal with a pilot expansion for Feature Y. Why: 1) measurable TTV improvement, 2) roadmap alignment reduces maintenance overhead"

3) Momentum story (3 slides)
- Slide A: Adoption curve (DAU/WAU) + top 3 power users
- Slide B: Feature adoption — wins (tickets resolved, time saved)
- Slide C: Case study vignette: internal use-case showing value
- Speaker note: "Call out the ripple: where the platform moved from exploratory to production usage."

4) Business metrics / ROI (2 slides)
- Slide: Key KPIs (requests/day, avg latency, 99p latency, token spend, cost per inference) with delta vs. prior quarter
- Speaker note: "Translate tokens into dollars and business outcomes — e.g., X tokens saved per month => $Y monthly cost reduction"

5) Risk & Blockers (1 slide)
- Table: Risk, impact, owner, mitigation, ETA
- Numeric thresholds (sample rubric):
  - Healthy (Green): Renewal risk score 0–3
  - Watch (Amber): 4–6
  - High (Red): 7–10
- Speaker note: "We want to resolve Amber items within 30 days. Anything Red requires executive touch."

6) Roadmap alignment (1 slide)
- Show 90-day product roadmap items mapped to customer blockers
- Speaker note: "This slide demonstrates how near-term releases directly lower the customer's operational burden."

7) Renewal Options (1 slide)
- Option A: Standard renewal — term, price, and minimal SLA
- Option B: Commit + Discount — 12m commit on Dedicated capacity, 10% discount + reserved throughput
- Option C: Enterprise — multi-year + professional services + extended support
- Speaker note: "We present a default but be ready to flex to Option B if they prioritize predictability."

8) Ask + next steps (1 slide)
- Clear action list: owner, due date, success criteria
- Speaker note: "Propose a decision window: agree to terms by [date], with a follow-up exec touch on [date]."

9) Appendix: Scenario bank and scripts (multiple short snippets)
- Script: Renew — Low friction
  - Opening: "You've seen steady gains and the suggested renewal keeps headroom for expected Q1 usage. Our ask is a 12-month renewal with the same terms."
  - Handling price pushback: "We can structure a pilot expansion with a performance SLA that reduces unit cost if usage grows X%."

- Script: Watch/Amber — Needs intervention
  - Opening: "We see strong feature adoption, but there are two operational gaps that could impair scale. Today I'd like to propose a focused remediation plan and an executive checkpoint in 30 days."
  - If they ask for concessions: "We can do a short-term credit during remediation, tied to milestone delivery."

- Script: High risk / Exec escalation
  - Opening: "We understand the urgency; we'd like to propose three immediate actions: 1) dedicated SE commitment for 2 weeks, 2) weekly executive sync, 3) a revised SLA for P1s. Let's aim for an interim decision by [date]."
  - Speaker note: "Be explicit about what 'immediate' means and who from our side will own it."

Renewal Risk Rubric (sample)
- Categories (each 0–3 points): Product stability, Business integration, Exec engagement, Value realization, Cost sensitivity
- Scoring guide: 0 = no concern, 1 = minor, 2 = moderate, 3 = major
- Quick math: total 0–15. Map to action: 0–4 continue standard cadence; 5–9 CSM + AE action plan; 10+ Exec escalation.

Renewal Tracker (mini-spec)
- Columns (suggested): Customer, ARR, Renewal date, Risk score, Past quarter change %, Top 3 blockers, Last touch (date), Next action (owner + date), Proposed option, Legal status
- Suggested filters: next 60 days, risk >= 5, ARR >= $50k
- Note: we keep a canonical sheet in CS Ops (link in linked artifacts) and pull into the QBR deck via a copy-paste table or automated report.

Customization checklist (to tailor templates)
- Replace generic screenshots with customer data (usage graphs)
- Recalculate ROI slide with customer-specific cost assumptions
- Confirm legal contact and procurement timeline before presenting enterprise options
- Add customer success story quote or internal stakeholder quote if available

Appendix: Data sources and definitions
- Usage: product telemetry (events-service), aggregated in CS-analytics daily exports
- Latency metrics: observability/tracing dashboard (link to observability page)
- Cost: finance chargeback report (monthly) — confirm with finance before quoting savings

Open questions / TODOs
- Create a one-pager cheat sheet for AEs that summarizes the script variants (Ethan action item).
- Add a slide template for token-cost-to-dollar conversion (Sofia) — include sample calculation.
- Request legal to draft a standardized 90-day remediation addendum for enterprise renewals (Liam).

Notes to self (tone intentionally informal)
- Keep executive slides tight: one metric, one takeaway per bullet.
- Practice the price-concession script — default to a performance milestone, not a flat discount.
- For enterprise QBRs, reserve 10–15 minutes for Exec-only conversation where we surface strategic alignment and risk.

References
- Confluence: QBR Playbook Index (linked above)
- Tracker canonical sheet: CS Ops / Renewals Tracker
- Related Jira tickets: CS-482 (renewal automation), CS-517 (remediation addendum)

Document history
- v0.1 (2025-11-03) initial draft
- v0.2 (2025-11-18) added rubric + scripts
- v0.3 (2025-12-05) incorporated collaborator feedback and TODOs

End of doc

-- Priya (CS)
